entry.title: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
entry.summary:
Demand on blockchain-based marketplaces arrives in bursts and at a high rate. On these platforms the data are completely visible, which makes it feasible to compare the bursty demand against the usual load. The congestion manifests as an increased demand for gas, the primary resource a blockchain sells.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance

entry.title: Beliefs Over Contracts -- by Francis Annan, Collin B. Raymond. We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects.
entry.summary:
We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects. Using a survey of managerial beliefs and a large-scale field experiment, we randomly assign agents at the market level to several widely used, expenditure-equivalent incentive schemes. In the field, the best-performing contract raises weekly firm profit by over 55% relative to the status quo, despite being ranked lower by managers, whereas the worst-performing contract performs as predicted.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #agents

entry.title: Strategic Monetary Policy in Open Economies -- by Louphou Coulibaly, Charles Engel
entry.summary:
We examine optimal non-cooperative monetary policy in a two-country New Keynesian setting with complete financial markets and pricing to market for goods. In contrast to the case in which the law of one price holds for goods, currency misalignments are an important consideration even for self-oriented policymakers. Financial markets are critical in the analysis.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: The Occupational Ladder: Implications for Life-Cycle Wage Dynamics -- by Henry E. Siu, Kelly Foley, Matias Cortes
entry.summary:
Some occupations pay higher wages than others, even conditional on worker characteristics, implying that occupations can be ranked on a ladder. We develop a simple decomposition to study the role this occupational ladder plays in average wage growth and in the fanning out of wages over the life cycle. We present three main findings.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: College Success: Understanding the Roles of Financial Aid, Loans, Preparation, and Incentives -- by Douglas N. Harris, Christopher R. Taber, Alan Yang
entry.summary:
Over the past four decades, the earnings gap between college graduates and non-graduates has widened substantially, prompting interest in policies aimed at promoting higher education among low-income students. A key challenge for these policies is the high college dropout rate. This paper develops a dynamic model of college enrollment and completion with rich individual heterogeneity to assess how various factors influence college attendance, dropout, and graduation.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: We Just Created More Than 1,000 Synthetic Controls To Study California's $20 Fast Food Minimum Wage -- by Jeffrey Clemens, Olivia Edwards, Jonathan Meer, Joshua D. Nguyen
entry.summary:
Synthetic control methods hold the promise of identifying a credible counterfactual by closely reproducing pretreatment outcome paths. Their reliability, however, depends in part on how effectively they constrain researchers’ less-visible degrees of freedom. We explore these methods’ sensitivity by constructing 1440 plausibly defensible specifications to estimate the employment effect of California’s $20 fast-food minimum wage.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics

entry.title: Insuring Landlords -- by Thomas Bézy, Antoine B. Levy, Timothy McQuade
entry.summary:
This paper shows that insuring landlords against non-payment risk can improve housing access and upward geographic mobility for fragile tenants. We study Visale, a large-scale publicly funded rent guarantee insurance policy in France, free for eligible tenants and landlords. Using administrative household and claim payout data and quasi-experimental eligibility variation by exact age, we show the guarantee increased access to private-sector rental housing, especially for immigrants, newly formed households, and low-income renters.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #combinatorics
